blocks.content: Rank States/UTs by number of establishments. Andhra Pradesh leads on Establishments at 611, followed by Maharashtra (582) and West Bengal (525). At the other end, Kerala records the lowest value at 204. The leader's Establishments is about 3.0 times that of the lowest-ranked unit, indicating a pronounced spread across the distribution. The top three units cluster closely, sharing the upper band of the distribution.

Aggregate establishments by region. South leads on Establishments at 1,874, followed by East (1,131) and North (1,079). At the other end, North-East records the lowest value at 373. The leader's Establishments is about 5.0 times that of the lowest-ranked unit, indicating a pronounced spread across the distribution.
Rural versus urban establishment split. The accompanying chart and table present the detailed breakdown for this indicator across the reported units.

Rank States/UTs by rural establishments. Andhra Pradesh leads on Rural Establishments at 350, followed by Maharashtra (321) and West Bengal (293). At the other end, Odisha records the lowest value at 106. The leader's Rural Establishments is about 3.3 times that of the lowest-ranked unit, indicating a pronounced spread across the distribution. The top three units cluster closely, sharing the upper band of the distribution.

Rank States/UTs by urban establishments. Andhra Pradesh leads on Urban Establishments at 261, followed by Maharashtra (261) and West Bengal (232). At the other end, Punjab records the lowest value at 97. The leader's Urban Establishments is about 2.7 times that of the lowest-ranked unit, indicating a pronounced spread across the distribution. The top three units cluster closely, sharing the upper band of the distribution.

Rank States/UTs by urban establishment share. Sikkim leads on Urban Establishments at 58.30, followed by Meghalaya (58.10) and Mizoram (54.50). At the other end, Telangana records the lowest value at 48.20. The top three units cluster closely, sharing the upper band of the distribution. The corresponding all-India figure for Urban Establishments stands at 44.50.

Rank regions by rural establishment share. Central leads on Rural Establishments at 56.20, followed by West (56.10) and South (55.60). At the other end, North-East records the lowest value at 54.40. The top three units cluster closely, sharing the upper band of the distribution. The corresponding all-India figure for Rural Establishments stands at 55.50.

Rank States/UTs by persons employed. Andhra Pradesh leads on Persons Working at 1,704, followed by Maharashtra (1,655) and West Bengal (1,389). At the other end, Punjab records the lowest value at 570. The leader's Persons Working is about 3.0 times that of the lowest-ranked unit, indicating a pronounced spread across the distribution. The top three units cluster closely, sharing the upper band of the distribution.

Aggregate employment by region. South leads on Persons Working at 5,182, followed by East (3,182) and North (3,076). At the other end, North-East records the lowest value at 1,040. The leader's Persons Working is about 5.0 times that of the lowest-ranked unit, indicating a pronounced spread across the distribution.

Rank regions by average employment per establishment. North leads on Avg Employment at 23.19, followed by North-East (23.04) and South (20.94). At the other end, West records the lowest value at 8.25. The leader's Avg Employment is about 2.8 times that of the lowest-ranked unit, indicating a pronounced spread across the distribution. The top three units cluster closely, sharing the upper band of the distribution.

Rank States/UTs by average employment. Meghalaya leads on Avg Employment at 3.26, followed by Odisha (3.20) and Himachal Pradesh (3.18). At the other end, Jharkhand records the lowest value at 2.92. The top three units cluster closely, sharing the upper band of the distribution.

Rank States/UTs by female workers. Andhra Pradesh leads on Female Workers at 269, followed by Maharashtra (266) and West Bengal (224). At the other end, Kerala records the lowest value at 105. The leader's Female Workers is about 2.6 times that of the lowest-ranked unit, indicating a pronounced spread across the distribution. The top three units cluster closely, sharing the upper band of the distribution.

Aggregate female workers by region. South leads on Female Workers at 829, followed by East (529) and North (495). At the other end, North-East records the lowest value at 166. The leader's Female Workers is about 5.0 times that of the lowest-ranked unit, indicating a pronounced spread across the distribution.

Rank States/UTs by female worker share. Lakshadweep leads on Female Workers at 42.10, followed by Nagaland (22.80) and Kerala (19.10). At the other end, Haryana records the lowest value at 16.10. The leader's Female Workers is about 2.6 times that of the lowest-ranked unit, indicating a pronounced spread across the distribution. The corresponding all-India figure for Female Workers stands at 15.90.

Rank regions by female worker share. East leads on Female Workers at 16.60, followed by North (16.10) and South (16). At the other end, Central records the lowest value at 15.10. The top three units cluster closely, sharing the upper band of the distribution. The corresponding all-India figure for Female Workers stands at 15.90.

Rank States/UTs by hired workers. Andhra Pradesh leads on Hired Workers at 985, followed by Maharashtra (941) and Uttar Pradesh (758). At the other end, Bihar records the lowest value at 353. The leader's Hired Workers is about 2.8 times that of the lowest-ranked unit, indicating a pronounced spread across the distribution. The top three units cluster closely, sharing the upper band of the distribution.

Rank States/UTs by hired worker share. Meghalaya leads on Hired Workers at 66.30, followed by Tripura (66.10) and Punjab (63.90). At the other end, Uttar Pradesh records the lowest value at 57.80. The top three units cluster closely, sharing the upper band of the distribution. The corresponding all-India figure for Hired Workers stands at 56.40.
Own-account versus hired-worker establishment mix. The corresponding all-India figure for Own Account Establishments stands at 61.70.

Rank States/UTs by own-account share. Arunachal Pradesh leads on Own Account Establishments at 71.40, followed by Andaman & Nicobar Islands (71.40) and Madhya Pradesh (68.60). At the other end, Kerala records the lowest value at 63.20. The top three units cluster closely, sharing the upper band of the distribution. The corresponding all-India figure for Own Account Establishments stands at 61.70.

Rank States/UTs by child workers. Maharashtra leads on Child Workers at 11, followed by Andhra Pradesh (10) and Tamil Nadu (7). At the other end, Bihar records the lowest value at 3. The leader's Child Workers is about 3.7 times that of the lowest-ranked unit, indicating a pronounced spread across the distribution.

Aggregate child workers by region. South leads on Child Workers at 22, followed by North (17) and West (15). At the other end, North-East records the lowest value at 8. The leader's Child Workers is about 2.8 times that of the lowest-ranked unit, indicating a pronounced spread across the distribution.

Rank States/UTs by child worker share. Delhi leads on Child Workers at 1.60, followed by Assam (1.10) and Manipur (1.10). At the other end, Tamil Nadu records the lowest value at 0.50. The leader's Child Workers is about 3.2 times that of the lowest-ranked unit, indicating a pronounced spread across the distribution. The corresponding all-India figure for Child Workers stands at 0.50.

Establishment base by region. South leads on Establishments at 1,874, followed by East (1,131) and North (1,079). At the other end, North-East records the lowest value at 373. The leader's Establishments is about 5.0 times that of the lowest-ranked unit, indicating a pronounced spread across the distribution.

Employment base by region. South leads on Persons Working at 5,182, followed by East (3,182) and North (3,076). At the other end, North-East records the lowest value at 1,040. The leader's Persons Working is about 5.0 times that of the lowest-ranked unit, indicating a pronounced spread across the distribution.

Average employment per establishment (synthesis). North leads on Avg Employment at 23.19, followed by North-East (23.04) and South (20.94). At the other end, West records the lowest value at 8.25. The leader's Avg Employment is about 2.8 times that of the lowest-ranked unit, indicating a pronounced spread across the distribution. The top three units cluster closely, sharing the upper band of the distribution.
